metadata.title: Claude, Finding It
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): opens on the hesitant writer + terms card, no verdict card; Your Turn is the Claude.ai composer; spoken outro stays.
metadata.audience: Practitioners and makers following the channel's Claude workflows

beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. In any organization, someone already wrote down the answer you need. The question isn't whether it exists — it's whether you can reach it.

shot.motion_claim: The writer types the naive file-search question and corrects it to the real one: reaching what the company already knows.

show.event: types 'Can I ask Claude to search our company files,'
backspaces 'search our company files' and replaces with 'retrieve what the company already knows' on the spoken correction

props.text:
Can I ask Claude to search our company files,
or is that too much to ask?
props.replacementWords: retrieve what the company already knows

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. Enterprise search: Claude searching inside your documents across all your connected sources at once. Content search: matching your question against what's actually on the page, not the filename. And access boundary: you only ever reach what you're already cleared to see.

show.event: 'enterprise search' term lands
'content search' term lands
'access boundary' term lands

terms.meaning: Claude searching inside your documents across all your connected sources at once
matching your question against what's actually on the page, not the filename
you only ever reach what you're already cleared to see

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: three prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: In any organization running for more than a year, the knowledge you need already exists. Someone wrote the pricing rationale. Someone documented the onboarding. The vendor terms are in an email. It all exists — scattered across three or four different systems — and you can't get to it.

shot.visual_intent: Three isometric server stacks (labeled Drive, Wiki, Chat) sit in separate corners of the cream stage. From the start, label 'scattered' sits below center — visible at midpoint. Kraft pages drift between the stacks with no connecting cables or paths. A question mark hovers at center stage.
shot.motion_claim: Scattered pages drift between three disconnected server stacks — the knowledge exists but has no route from a question to an answer.

show.event: three server stacks appear at stage corners, labeled Drive, Wiki, Chat; label 'scattered' below center
pages drift between stacks — no connections, no cables
question mark grows at center stage
pages still drifting, question mark holds

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn isometric scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Underfill and clustered waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Normal file search matches the label. You called the file 'Q3 notes' — it holds your decision to switch payment processors. Search 'payment processor' and the file never surfaces. The name and the content have nothing to do with each other.

shot.visual_intent: A kraft box lands center stage. Its top face is labeled 'Q3-notes' in ink — visible from the first frame. A terracotta scan line sweeps left-to-right across the box label. The ink query label 'payment processor' approaches from the left and drifts off the right edge — no match. Label 'names lie' below the box.
shot.motion_claim: A terracotta scan sweeps a kraft box label and the query drifts off stage with no match — filename search misses the content inside.

show.event: kraft box labeled 'Q3-notes' drops and settles; label 'names lie' below
terracotta scan line sweeps across the box label
ink query label 'payment processor' approaches from left then drifts off the right edge
box and label hold; query gone

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn isometric scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Underfill and clustered waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Content search reads what's on the page. It matches your question against the actual words, not the label on the folder. That file with the wrong name? It surfaces the right sentence.

shot.visual_intent: Continuity from B01: the same 'Q3-notes' kraft box is on stage. The lid lifts off. Pages fan out of the box, each showing ink text lines. An ink scan sweeps the text lines on the leading page. A terracotta dot lands on a matching line — the payoff. Label 'reads inside' beside the page.
shot.motion_claim: The box opens, pages fan, a terracotta dot lands on a content line — content search finds the sentence, not the label.

show.event: lid lifts off the kraft box (continuity from B01)
pages fan out; ink text lines visible on the leading page
ink scan sweeps the text lines
terracotta dot lands on the matching line; label 'reads inside' beside the page

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn isometric scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Underfill and clustered waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: And it searches all your sources simultaneously — your drive, your wiki, your shared folders, your chat. You don't need to remember where you put something. You only need to remember roughly what it was about.

shot.visual_intent: Three server stacks (Drive, Wiki, Chat) — same cast as B00 — at left, center-right, and right. Label 'all at once' appears below center from the start. An ink arc radiates outward from a center origin and reaches all three stacks simultaneously. A terracotta dot lights on each stack at the moment the arc touches it.
shot.motion_claim: A single ink arc radiates and touches three source stacks at once, each lighting with a terracotta dot — one question, simultaneous reach.

show.event: three server stacks on stage; label 'all at once' below center
ink arc expands from center origin, reaching all three stacks simultaneously
terracotta dot lights on each stack as the arc touches it
all three stacks lit; arc holds

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn isometric scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Underfill and clustered waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Most document archives are a graveyard — things go in, nothing comes back out. Connect enterprise search and the same pile becomes a resource you can ask questions of.

shot.visual_intent: A 2x3 grid of page stacks on stage from the first frame, labeled 'archive' at top — ensuring a label is up at midpoint. All stacks start in ghost grey (dim, dormant). One by one, left to right, terracotta dots appear on each stack and the stacks shift from ghost grey to warm kraft tone. Label 'living archive' replaces 'archive' when all are lit.
shot.motion_claim: Grey dormant page stacks light up row by row as terracotta dots appear — the graveyard becomes a living archive.

show.event: grid of grey page stacks; label 'archive' at top
terracotta dots appear one by one; each stack shifts from ghost to kraft
all stacks lit; label becomes 'living archive'

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn isometric scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Underfill and clustered waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: When the plugin finds the document you need, it can pull that content straight into the conversation. Ask about your pricing strategy — it retrieves your own pricing analysis and reasons from it. That's the difference between generic advice and advice grounded in your actual data.

shot.visual_intent: A server stack on left labeled 'sources'. An open-top kraft box on right labeled 'conversation'. Both labels visible from the first frame. A kraft page lifts from the server stack, arcs through the air using MoveAlongPath (not animate path_arc), and slides into the conversation box. A terracotta dot appears on the conversation box when the page lands. Label 'pulled in' beside the conversation box.
shot.motion_claim: A found page lifts from the server stack and arcs into the conversation box — content pulled straight into context, grounding the answer in real data.

show.event: server stack ('sources') and open conversation box on stage; labels visible
page lifts from the server stack
page arcs and slides into the conversation box via MoveAlongPath
terracotta dot appears on the box; label 'pulled in' lands beside it

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn isometric scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Underfill and clustered waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Five workflows unlock this. Institutional memory: why did we make that decision? Client context: where did things stand with that person? Policy lookup: what are our standard terms? Meeting prep: what do we already know about who we're meeting? And contradiction check: have we quoted this before, and at what price?

shot.visual_intent: A central hub box at center stage — visible from the start. Five kraft pages drop in one at a time and fan around the hub in a row (not diagonal — to avoid bounding-box overlap that GATE T reads as stacked labels). Each page is labeled in ink: 'Memory', 'Context', 'Policy', 'Prep', 'No repeats'. Pages arrive on the spoken workflow name. A terracotta dot appears on the hub when the fifth page lands.
shot.motion_claim: Five labeled pages drop in on the spoken workflow name and fan around a hub — one page per workflow, the cast enacting the five use cases.

show.event: central hub box on stage
page 'Memory' drops to the left of hub
page 'Context' drops beside it
page 'Policy' drops beside it
page 'Prep' drops beside it
page 'No repeats' drops; terracotta dot on hub; all five fanned in a row

beats.narration_text: Here's the line. The plugin searches only what you can already see. Your credentials, your permissions — nothing new. It can't reach a document you couldn't open yourself. It reaches what you already can, faster.

shot.visual_intent: A small ink dot at center labeled 'search' — visible from the first frame to satisfy GATE T midpoint. A terracotta arc expands outward from the dot (terracotta as 'one curve' per palette rule). At roughly 60% of the beat, the arc reaches a bright ink ring labeled 'your access' and stops hard. Ghost-grey page stacks sit outside the ring. Label 'nothing beyond' appears outside the ring.
shot.motion_claim: A terracotta search arc expands then stops at an ink boundary ring — you reach only what you're already cleared to see, and nothing beyond.

show.event: ink dot at center stage, labeled 'search'
terracotta arc expands outward from the dot
arc reaches the bright ink ring labeled 'your access' and stops
ghost-grey stacks visible outside the ring; label 'nothing beyond' outside

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn isometric scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Underfill and clustered waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: It does nothing until you connect it. Point it at wherever your important documents live. The first index takes a while — after that, searches are fast.

shot.visual_intent: Three source boxes on left labeled 'Drive', 'Wiki', 'Chat'. A central empty index box on the right labeled 'index' — both sets visible from frame one. Streams of tiny page-dots (ink, small) flow from each source box to the index box. The index box fills with dots rising like a level. A terracotta check-dot appears on the index when full. Label 'connected' beside the index.
shot.motion_claim: Page-dot streams flow from three labeled source boxes into a central index that fills and resolves with a check — connect once, then search fast.

show.event: three source boxes (Drive, Wiki, Chat) and empty index box on stage; labels visible
page-dot streams flow from each source into the index
index fills
terracotta check-dot appears on the index; label 'connected' lands

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style (Bear, 2026-09-26): one drawn isometric scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Underfill and clustered waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: The superpower is synthesis. Ask what approaches you've tried for client onboarding — file search hands you files. This combines several documents into one coherent answer. You can't do that with a folder search.

shot.visual_intent: Three kraft pages on the left, labeled 'sources' as a group label from the first frame. Ink arrows draw from each page converging to a center point. A single larger merged page emerges on the right of the convergence point. A terracotta dot appears on the merged page. Label 'combined' beside the merged page.
shot.motion_claim: Three pages converge via ink arrows into one merged answer page — synthesis beats plain file retrieval.

show.event: three kraft pages on left; group label 'sources' above them
ink arrows draw from each page toward a center convergence point
merged page appears to the right of the convergence point
terracotta dot on the merged page; label 'combined' beside it

beats.narration_text: And the return compounds. Every time you note why you chose something — the vendor with the lower international fees, say — thirty seconds now becomes a searchable asset that saves an hour a year from now. The archive is only as good as what you feed it.

shot.visual_intent: An open kraft archive box with a small page stack on the right side of the stage. Label 'archive' on the box from the first frame. An ink cursor arrow on the left side of the stage. The cursor moves (MoveAlongPath, not animate path_arc) carrying a new kraft page card toward the box and drops it in. The page stack inside grows taller. Label 'tomorrow's source' appears beside the growing stack.
shot.motion_claim: A cursor drops a new page into the archive box; the stack grows taller — documenting now compounds into future search value.

show.event: archive box with small stack on stage, labeled 'archive'; ink cursor with page card on left
cursor moves toward box via MoveAlongPath and drops the page in
stack grows taller inside the box
label 'tomorrow's source' appears beside the growing stack

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Help me set up enterprise search for my team. First, ask me which tools our documents actually live in — drive, wiki, shared folders, chat. Then tell me the three questions I should try first to prove it works, and one decision I should start documenting this week so it's searchable later. Then check two things yourself: does Claude actually reach every source you named? And what's one decision you made last week that's now written down?
